name: Reducto
verdict: No OAuth: you use your own key from Studio and send customer documents under your account, about 1-3 days. A customer who wants their own account pastes their key, and enterprise terms likely need sales.
needGuide: No — just create an API key in Studio and store it server-side.

auth.detail: Reducto is a document-parsing API, not a user-data app. API keys are created in Studio and sent as `Authorization: Bearer $REDUCTO_API_KEY` to https://platform.reducto.ai. The hosted MCP server (https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp) also takes the API key as a bearer token. The local MCP server's `--login` uses a browser device-code flow only to fetch and save a key. No OAuth app registration for third parties.

approval.gate: None for OAuth because none exists. You use your own key (your customers' documents are sent to Reducto under your account). Enterprise terms, zero-retention or higher limits likely need a Reducto sales contact (unconfirmed).

scopes.why: Keys are all-or-nothing for the account.
scopes.summary: None. Keys are all-or-nothing for the account; no per-scope model documented.

cost: Free signup with credits (amount not stated); usage billed in credits
prerequisites: Account and owner: Anyone who can sign up at Studio. Use a company-owned account so keys are not tied to a personal email.
Where you register: studio.reducto.ai → sign up → sidebar API Keys → create key, name it and copy.
Cost: Free signup with credits (amount not stated); usage billed in credits

registerAt.path: studio.reducto.ai → sign up → sidebar API Keys → create key, name it and copy.

steps.do: Sign up at studio.reducto.ai with a company email.
Open API Keys in the Studio sidebar, create a key named for the environment and store it in a secrets manager.
Call POST https://platform.reducto.ai/upload and /parse with the Bearer key or via the Python/Node/Go SDK (reads REDUCTO_API_KEY).
For agent tooling, add the hosted MCP server with an Authorization: Bearer header, or run `uvx mcp-server-reducto`.
If supporting bring-your-own-key, add a settings field that stores the customer's key encrypted and validates it with a test parse.
Review data-processing terms and retention for customer documents.

roles.team: Anyone who can sign up at Studio. Use a company-owned account so keys are not tied to a personal email.
roles.customer: Customers do not connect an account. If a customer wants to bring their own key, they create it in Studio and paste it into your app.

testing: Free Studio account; each parse response reports credits used in usage.credits.
Rate limits not stated in the quickstart.

blockers.problem: No OAuth, so customers cannot connect their own account
blockers.fix: Use your own key or a BYO-key field.

blockers.problem: Customer documents are processed under your account
blockers.fix: Cover this in your DPA and ask Reducto about retention options.

blockers.problem: Rate limits and credit amounts are not documented in the quickstart
blockers.fix: Check the account dashboard or contact Reducto.

automation.agentCan: Write the parse client, configure MCP, run test parses, and build the BYO-key form and validation call.
automation.humanMust: Sign up, create and rotate the key, accept terms, add payment, and sign any enterprise or data-handling agreement.

uncertain: Rate limits, free credit amount, SOC2/retention options, and whether Reducto offers OAuth on request were not found.
